text:
morgan: seeing a small cluster of apiserver 502/503s in ap-southeast2 starting ~09:07 UTC after the GPU autoscaler finished a big burst. apiserver logs show a ton of watch timeouts and long queue processing

sam: ugh. did the scaleout attach NVMe snapshot jobs or anything heavy?

morgan: looks like a mix — a couple of large model pull jobs hit the nodes and there was a flurry of webhook/controller churn. i grabbed kube-apiserver stderr: 
```
I0311 09:07:24.123] watchCache: exceeded max processing time - processing took 2.3s (threshold 0.5s)
E0311 09:07:25.456] apiserver: write tcp 10.4.0.12:6443->10.4.2.7:51234: write: connection reset by peer
```

li: controller-manager logs? leader election flips?

morgan: yes — controller-manager shows repeated leader-loss and immediate restart: 
```
I0311 09:07:30 leader-election: obtaining lease redwood-system/controller-manager...
E0311 09:07:31 controller-runtime.leader: lost lock due to etcd timeout: context deadline exceeded
```

devon: that smells like etcd-side latency, maybe IO or conntrack limits on proxies. infra-bot, any infra alerts in that window?

infra-bot: [ALERT] 09:05-09:12 ap-southeast2 NAT gateway conntrack high-water (80% of table), node nvme iops spiking on gpu-pool-3, transient route flaps observed on bgp-peer-2

sam: conntrack + nvme iops + big model pulls = apiserver writes/reads slow -> watch queue stalls -> controllers lose lead. we saw similar pattern in eu1 last year but with different root cause.

li: quick mitigation: reduce read pressure to etcd by pinning nodes to local model cache or scale down bursty jobs. can we temporarily cordon the new GPU nodes and fall back to older pool?

morgan: i'm on it — cordoning gpu-pool-3 now and setting autoscaler min to previous baseline. running: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-pool-3-*`

sam: also bump etcd heartbeat/snapshot windows? longer-term we should consider moving model pulls off the controlplane overlay (separate network) or throttle image pulls during leader elections.

devon: for immediate triage, let's rotate etcd leader to a less-loaded replica and check disk queue depth. @li can you check `iostat -x` on etcd nodes and collect dstat from 09:00-09:10?

li: grabbing iostat now — attaching a quick sample: 
```
Device            r/s     w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.3  1024.1  512.0 122880.0   240.0    28.1  1.23  95.2
```

li: %util ~95 on the primary etcd NVMe during the spike. controller-manager leader flips line up with nvme saturation.

morgan: ok i left one node cordoned and scaled down the batch job CR (model-deployments/big-v2) to 0 replicas. watch errors dropped almost immediately and apiserver 2xx rate recovering.

sam: good. action items: 1) investigate why GPU pool pulls were routed through same NAT/egress path as etcd traffic (infra network pathing) 2) tune conntrack for NAT gateway or provision additional NAT capacity 3) surface a policy so model pulls during autoscale use a separate subnet or pre-warmed cache 4) consider etcd I/O QoS on NVMe devices.

devon: i'll own NAT / conntrack scaling and routing change, opening infra ticket. li, can you open a perf ticket for etcd I/O QoS and leader placement heuristics?

li: on it, will include the iostat samples and apiserver/watch logs.

morgan: i'll write a short postmortem draft and link the action items, include who did what during the mitigation.

sam: ping me for prioritization — this impacts Dedicated customers' SLAs if we don't harden. also add a short-term alert: if nvme %util > 85 and controller-manager leader flips > 3 in 5m, alert pagers.

devon: updated NAT autoscale policy -> provisioning new NATIPs now, should reduce conntrack pressure once they attach (~5m).

infra-bot: [INFO] 09:13 NATIPs allocated -> 3 new IPs attaching to ap-southeast2-nat-gw-1

morgan: apiserver 200-rate steady now, controller-manager leader stable. will follow up with ticket links and docs for gated model pull policy. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: nice work. we'll schedule a short blameless review tomorrow 10:30 UTC to decide the long-term approach.

li: adding docs link for possible QoS options: https://internal.docs/etcd-io-qos

morgan: end thread — saving logs to incident-archive/3554443210
